parts.note: getting hitched is marrying, and a post is a job or office, so this is the place where civil weddings are performed

explanation.definitionFit: A civil wedding takes place at this municipal building, so it is where couples get hitched.

indicators.note: replacement suggests the letters put back in a different order

parts.note: taken as written, possessive S included

explanation.surface: Someone protests at the man brought in to stand in for Ernest.
explanation.definitionFit: To resent something is to take objection to it.

clue.text: Eager, ready and equal to winning at tennis

parts.note: game means willing or eager
set means ready, as in 'ready, steady, go'
taken as written
a match is an equal, as in 'no match for'

explanation.surface: A tennis player is keen, prepared and good enough to win.
explanation.definitionFit: The umpire's call ending a tennis match announces the winner has taken it.

indicators.note: Sound signals that a word is pronounced like another

parts.note: sight is one of the five senses

explanation.surface: Pondering whether one's sense of place is reliable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' looks like 'sensible' but signals a word heard; 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A site is a location or position where something stands.

clue.text: Discover a doctor breaking the law

indicators.note: breaking suggests one piece forcing its way into another

parts.note: a rule is a law
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: Finding out that a physician has broken the law.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Discover' is the definition in the British slang sense of seeing through a scheme; 'breaking' is the container signal and 'a' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To rumble someone is British slang for finding them out or discovering their deceit.

clue.text: How the skipper may be caught unawares?

definitions.text: How the skipper may be caught unawares?

parts.words: How the skipper may be caught unawares?
parts.note: a skipper here is something that hops, like a flea or kangaroo, caught in mid-jump, i.e. off guard

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means unprepared or by surprise, literally caught while hopping.

clue.text: Be like others and keep up with court action

parts.note: to follow is to keep up with, track
a suit is a lawsuit, an action in court

explanation.surface: Conform, and keep abreast of a legal case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' is a link. In card games the phrase means playing the same suit as the lead.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means doing what someone else has just done, conforming.

clue.text: Source reference provided before start of the lesson

definitions.text: Source reference provided before start of the lesson

parts.words: Source reference provided before start of the lesson
parts.note: a church reading is introduced with the book, section and line numbers of the Bible passage

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means a precise citation of source, from Bible references read out before a lesson.

clue.text: Cut over a quarter? That's serious

indicators.note: in a down clue, over places the first piece above the second

parts.note: to sever is to cut
E, east, is one of the four quarters of the compass

explanation.surface: Asking whether cutting something by a quarter is grave.
explanation.definitionFit: Severe means grave or serious, as in a severe illness.

clue.text: Tommy's quiet, possibly a sign of illness

indicators.note: possibly signals that the letters may be arranged in some other order

parts.note: taken as written, the possessive S included
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, quiet

explanation.surface: A normally lively boy called Tommy has gone quiet, which may mean he is unwell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges TOMMYSP (Tommy's plus P) into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A symptom is an indication of disease noticed in a patient.

parts.note: till means up to, as in 'till Monday'
an age or period of time is a date in history, an era

explanation.surface: A question whether farming practice is modern.
explanation.definitionFit: Tillage is the ploughing and preparing of land for crops, i.e. cultivation.

parts.note: not a children's den but the home a bird builds in a tree

explanation.definitionFit: Birds build their homes in branches, so a bird's dwelling is literally a house in a tree.

definitions.meaning: a large buzzing blowfly with a metallic blue body
old slang for a police officer, from the blue uniform

explanation.definitionFit: Both a blowfly and, in dated slang, a uniformed constable go by this name.

clue.text: Speaker swallows one drink as starter

indicators.note: swallows suggests one piece taking another inside it

parts.note: an orator is a public speaker
I is the Roman numeral one
gin is a drink

explanation.surface: A public speaker downs a drink before starting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swallows' puts IGIN inside ORATOR; 'as' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An originator is one who starts or initiates something.

parts.note: not someone taking part in activities but the stitch a surgeon uses to close a wound during surgery

explanation.definitionFit: A surgical stitch holds the edges of a wound together, joining tissue in an operation.

clue.text: Counters chaos, to put it into plain English

indicators.note: chaos suggests the letters thrown into disorder and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone tidies up a mess of counters before explaining things simply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chaos' rearranges the letters of 'Counters'; 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To construe a passage is to interpret or translate it, putting its meaning plainly.

clue.text: Get a role as someone's double

definitions.text: Get a role as someone's double

parts.words: Get a role as someone's double
parts.note: an actor cast as a character's second self, a hidden other personality

explanation.walkthrough: The letters of 'Get a role' rearrange to the answer, but no word signals an anagram, so it reads as a cryptic definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An alter ego is a second self or another side of a person, like a double.

clue.text: Tribute paid to Viking not entirely!

parts.note: the Danes were Viking raiders of England
an entire is an uncastrated horse, so to geld is to make one not entire

explanation.surface: Payment handed over to Norse raiders was only partial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Entire' here is the horse-breeder's word for an ungelded stallion; 'paid to' is a link. Danegeld was the levy raised in Anglo-Saxon England to buy off Viking attacks.
explanation.definitionFit: Danegeld was a tax or payment made to keep Danish invaders away, a form of tribute.

clue.text: It may provide a crash course for the fair driver

definitions.text: It may provide a crash course for the fair driver

parts.words: It may provide a crash course for the fair driver
parts.note: a fairground bumper car, which is driven around a track meant for collisions

explanation.definitionFit: A bumper car at a funfair is made for crashing into others on its course.

parts.note: to win is to have success
now means at once, immediately

explanation.surface: A supporter enjoys a victory straight away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fan' looks like a supporter but is the verb: to blow chaff from grain.
explanation.definitionFit: Winnowing grain means fanning it so the wind blows the chaff away.

parts.note: a well is a spring of water
to set something is to adjust it, as a clock

explanation.surface: A spring has been adjusted and now holds firm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spring' looks like a coil but is a water source; 'and' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Well-set means solidly built or firmly fixed in place.

parts.note: to do someone is to cheat or swindle them
a blushing face is red

explanation.surface: Being fond of someone after watching a swindler go red.
explanation.definitionFit: Adored means loved deeply.

parts.note: read 'Notable' as note-able: a musical marking telling players to grow softer

explanation.definitionFit: This musical direction instructs performers to reduce loudness gradually.

indicators.note: rejected suggests the word being turned back on itself

parts.note: to be is to live or exist

explanation.surface: Being turned down is a bad thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns LIVE backwards; 'that's' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Evil is wicked, morally bad.

clue.text: Classical maid who always had the last word

definitions.text: Classical maid who always had the last word

parts.words: Classical maid who always had the last word
parts.note: the nymph of Greek myth cursed to repeat only the final words others spoke

explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth this nymph could only repeat the closing words of others.

parts.note: read two ways: to grant someone a right, and to give someone a title or name

explanation.definitionFit: To entitle is both to confer a right on someone and to bestow a title.

definitions.meaning: written logs or archives in which things are noted
top achievements that have never been bettered, as in sport

explanation.definitionFit: Archives kept as logs, and best-ever marks set by athletes, share this name.

parts.note: not a garden bird's nest but the Nottinghamshire woodland of the outlaw Robin Hood

explanation.definitionFit: Legend places the outlaw Robin Hood and his band in this Nottinghamshire woodland.
